newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Israeli premier, Swiss president to meet in Davos.
newsitem.headline: Israeli premier, Swiss president to meet in Davos.

text.p: Swiss President Arnold Koller, his country under fire from Jewish groups over its World War Two role, will meet Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu at the World Economic Forum in Davos, officials said on Tuesday.
"They will meet. It will be more than just a handshake," Koller's spokesman told reporters.

The spokesman declined to say if the two leaders would discuss tensions between Switzerland and groups led by the World Jewish Congress over claims that Swiss banks may still be sitting on assets left ownerless by Jews killed in the Holocaust.

The spokesman also declined to say when exactly the two would meet during the annual gathering of world business and political leaders in the Alpine resort on January 30-February 4. Koller is due to attend the first two days.
Koller, who is also justice and police minister, started his one-year term as Swiss president this month, succeeding Economics Minister Jean-Pascal Delamuraz.
Delamuraz was earlier this month forced to apologise for calling Jewish compensation demands "blackmail".
Separately, Israeli President Ezer Weizman cancelled a planned visit to Switzerland, but officials said it was not because of the dispute between Jewish groups and the Swiss.

Israel's embassy in Berne said Weizman had dropped plans to attend on August 31 the 100th anniversary of the first Zionist congress, which met in the Swiss city of Basle and launched a movement that led to the founding of Israel in 1948.
"The reason is because of unforeseen problems that have arisen in his agenda," an embassy spokesman told Reuters.
"There is absolutely no connection between the cancellation of the visit and the issue of Holocaust victims' money," the spokesman added.
Weizman's decision also meant he would not meet Swiss government leaders in Berne as had been planned in connection with the Basle trip, the embassy spokesman said.
"The bilateral talks in Berne have been rescheduled, not cancelled," he said, adding that no alternative date had been set yet.

The spokesman said Israel Knesset (parliament) speaker Dan Tichon would take part in the Basle cermonies commemorating the first congress of the Zionist movement for a Jewish state started by Theodor Herzl.

Berne and Swiss banks agreed last week to set up a Holocaust memorial fund. But ties with Jewish organisations were strained this week by publication of a confidential report from Berne's ambassador in Washington that called for "waging war" against Jewish groups and other critics.
Ambassador Carlo Jagmetti resigned on Monday over the controversy, which added to tensions left by Delamuraz's blackmail comment despite his apology.
